description: VOORAANKONDIGING EUROPESE OPENBARE AANBESTEDING Dit betreft een vooraankondiging waarmee de gemeente Rotterdam de markt vroegtijdig wil informeren over een aankomende opdracht, nog vóórdat de eigenlijke aanbestedingsprocedure formeel van start gaat, zodat geinteresserde ondernemers zich kunnen voorbereiden. Bij een vooraankondiging kunnen partijen zich nog niet aanmelden, nog niet inschrijven, nog geen vragen stellen of formele aanbestedingsdocumentatie inzien. De werkelijke inschrijving kan pas zodra de officiële aanbesteding wordt gepubliceerd. De Bosdreef wordt in twee fasen naar het noorden verlegd om ruimte te maken voor de nieuwe woonwijk Nieuw Kralingen en een bedrijvenstrook. Fase 1 is opgeleverd in 2024. Op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 wordt de Europese openbare aanbesteding gepubliceerd voor de opgave van fase 2. Het doel van de Opdracht van fase 2 is de realisatie van fase 2 van de Verlegde Bosdreef als volwaardige noordelijke ontsluitingsroute (1x2-baansweg, 50 km/u) ter vervanging van de huidige Bosdreef (thans 2x2-baansweg, 70 km/u). De beoogde startdatum van de werkzaamheden in deze Opdracht fase 2 staat gepland op 1 februari 2027. De Opdracht die in de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure zal worden beschreven gaat over: Nieuw wegtracé (50 km/u-gebiedsontsluitingsweg) met fundering, verharding, markering en wegmeubilair Compleet rioleringssysteem (hemel- en vuilwater) aansluitend op bestaande infrastructuur Operationele VRI's en openbare verlichting Nieuwe, bredere betonnen Crooswijksebrug (niet-beweegbaar) Geïntegreerd infrastructuursysteem Volledige verbinding tussen fase 1 en fase 2 Vergunningen, keuringen, opleverdocumentatie en overdracht aan beheer (RAW-systematiek) Het werk bestaat in hoofdzaak uit : Grondwerk (ontgraven en ophogen inclusief verwerken) Het slopen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het bouwen van een betonnen brug (inclusief fundatie) Het aanbrengen van en grondkering (stalen damwand met verankering) Verwijderen asfaltverharding Aanbrengen asfaltverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen elementenverharding inclusief fundering Aanbrengen / installeren van een gemaal Aanleg DIT-riolering / riolering Aanleg persleiding Aanleg waterberging Aanleg verkeersregelinstallaties Aanleg installatie openbare verlichting Bijkomende werkzaamheden De bovenstaande opsomming van werkzaamheden is slechts een indicatie van de te verrichten werkzaamheden en alleen bedoeld om de interesse van potentiële Inschrijvers voor de Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure te wekken. Inschrijvers kunnen geen rechten ontlenen aan deze opsomming. Zie voor een nadere technische omschrijving van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden de aanbestedingsleidraad en het daarbij gevoegde RAW-bestek zoals dat op of omstreeks 19 juni 2026 zal worden gepubliceerd via dit Aanbestedingsplatform.

title: France – Site preparation work – Réalisation des travaux préparatoires à l’extension d’une installation nucléaire existante
description: Le CEA projette la construction d’un bâtiment d’extension d’une installation existante sur le centre de Valduc. Afin de garantir la parfaite préparation de l’emplacement retenu, le CEA souhaite, à travers le marché objet de ce présent avis, réaliser les travaux préparatoires nécessaires à l’aménagement de la zone de construction. Ces travaux correspondent aux prestations suivantes : - L’aménagement de la zone de chantier ; - La dépose et le dévoiement de réseaux existants sur la zone ; - Le réaménagement du merlon situé sur le bâtiment adjacent au futur bâtiment, y compris la dépose d’ouvrages existants ; - La réalisation de la plateforme du futur bâtiment et des futures bases vies pour la phase travaux ; - L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires ; - L’amenée de tous les réseaux nécessaires (dont Eaux Usées, Eaux Industriels, Eau Potable, Infrastructures pour Courants Forts et Courants Faibles Industriels). Les travaux du présent Marché correspondent aux travaux préparatoires préalables à la construction d’une extension d’un Bâtiment existant. Ces travaux comprennent en part ferme : • La zone d’installation chantier du Titulaire, y compris signalisation de chantier, • La réalisation des éléments assurant la délimitation de la future zone chantier qui comprend : o L’implantation des limitations des futurs ouvrages o La mise en place de clôtures et de barrières de protection o La réalisation de la plateforme et des sujétions associées au futur poste de gardiennage, y compris réseaux secs et humides • La dépose et/ou dévoiement de réseaux secs et humides (dont EP, EI, AEP, CFO, CFI,) • Le réaménagement du merlon du bâtiment existant avec les sujétions associées dont notamment : o La dépose du merlon (environ 7500m3) o La dépose d’ouvrages d’existants en béton armé (ouvrages de soutènement et galerie extérieure) o La réalisation de nouveaux ouvrages de soutènement en béton armé pour le merlon en toiture sur 50ml environ o La mise en bardage du voile extérieur du bâtiment existant, y compris toutes sujétions (60m x 12m environ) • L’aménagement de la plateforme de la future extension (environ 1500 m3 de déblai) (profondeur d’environ 1m) • L’aménagement de la zone des bases vie pour une surface approximative de 1300m² • L’évacuation des matériaux de déblai (zone de dépose sur le site à 1.5 km en aller simple) • La mise en place des réseaux, postes et équipements électriques pour le futur chantier depuis le bâtiment existant (1 armoire de distribution générale de chantier alimentant les bases vie, les grues et les coffrets de chantier) • La mise en place des arrivées de réseaux secs et humides pour les futures bases vies de chantier • La dépose et l’évacuation du poste électrique HT/BT existant et présent sur l’emprise chantier ainsi que les structures associées, y compris liaisons électriques • Un suivi géotechnique de type mission G3 • La pose de candélabres sur poteau bois avec haut-parleurs (environ une dizaine) • L’établissement de tous les documents nécessaires à la bonne exécution des travaux (études d’exécution, documents d’organisation de chantier...) mentionnés supra • La réalisation des contrôles et essais à réaliser pour les postes mentionnés supra • Le dossier des ouvrages exécutés Les prestations optionnelles à réaliser au titre du marché sont décrites infra. Les prestations prévues au BPU vont notamment concerner les domaines suivants : • Le détour d’un camion de terre de déblais par l’entrée du centre de Valduc pour contrôle radiologique (distance 6km en aller simple) • L’évacuation sur le site des matériaux de déblais excédentaires • Un arrêt de chantier d’un jour • Un arrêt de chantier d’une semaine ouvrée NOTA 1 : cette liste de prestations prévues au BPU n’est pas exhaustive. NOTA 2 : Les volumes précisés supra correspondent à des quantités estimées par le CEA. Elles ne constituent pas un engagement du CEA. Les prestations optionnelles du marché sont les suivantes : • L’agrandissement du bassin d’orage (130m3 maximum) • Alimentation des bases vie depuis un futur poste HT BT (hors périmètre de ce marché) (environ 200ml) Les prestations se déroulent sur le Centre CEA/DAM de VALDUC en Zone Protégée avec contraintes d’accès et d’exploitation.

title: Market Intelligence Notice: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station Taxiway A4 & Runway Extension Project - Use of Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) Utilizing Other Transaction Authority (OTA)
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / MARKET INTELLIGENCE NOTICE Place of Performance: Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS), New York Notice: This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market intelligence and for informational purposes only. This announcement does not constitute a Solicitation or a Request for Proposal (RFP), and no solicitation is currently available. Participation in this RFI is strictly voluntary. The Government will not be obligated to award any agreement or contract because of this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs associated with the preparation or submission of information. Submitting a response will not affect a firm�s ability to submit a proposal should formal solicitation be issued in the future. NAICS Code: 237310 � Highway, Street and Bridge Construction. (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction to extend Runway 10-28 and associated taxiways at the Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station, New York. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver fully functional airfield improvements. The primary project elements include: a. Reconstructing the existing overrun/blast pad on Runway 28 end to full-strength airfield pavement. b. Extending Runway 10-28 and extending Taxiway A4 to connect the 914th ARW apron to the new Runway 28 end. c. Extending a 520-foot portion of Runway 6-24 and providing a warmup pad for two (2) KC-135R aircraft. The potential total area of new airfield pavement is approximately 780,000 sq ft. d. Modifying the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Medium-Intensity Approach Lighting System with Runway End Identification Lights (MALSR) approach lighting, which requires active coordination with FAA construction representatives during removal and re-installation. e. Installing new airfield electrical and lighting systems, including runway edge lights, runway centerline lights, threshold lights, touchdown zone lights, airfield signage, and taxiway edge lights. f. Constructing a new creek culvert to allow the new taxiway to traverse the Cayuga Creek. g. Erecting a jet blast deflector fence on the Runway 28 end. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $50,000,000.00 CRITICAL PROJECT CONSTRAINTS & CHALLENGES: Geotechnical Constraints: The project site features variable and shallow bedrock (as shallow as 3 feet below grade) and a high groundwater table that heavily complicates subdrainage and stormwater design. Sensitive Environmental Conditions: Work will occur near federal and state-regulated wetlands and Cayuga Creek. The site is a habitat for the Devil Crayfish, which is listed as a species of Greatest Conservation Needs. Multiple permits with State and Federal agencies will be required prior to construction. Operational Constraints: A significant portion of the work will occur within the active runway Controlled Movement Area (CMA). Work requires compliance with an FAA-approved Construction Safety and Phasing Plan (CSPP), temporary displaced threshold markings, modifications to NAVAIDS, and FAA flight checks. Security Constraints: Strict security constraints are in place, requiring Government escorts at all times during construction. Airfield Pavement Quality Control: Onsite batch plant space (approx. 6 acres) has been identified. Review and final approval of concrete and asphalt mix designs reside with the USACE Transportation Service Center (TSC). The TSC will provide a mandatory, weeklong airfield pavement workshop prior to the start of construction, which the contractor�s key personnel must attend. Stakeholder Coordination: The contract requires active coordination with the airport operator (Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority - NFTA), USACE, Air Force Reserve Command (AFRC), FAA, and Niagara Falls Air Reserve Station (NFARS). PLANNED ACQUISITION STRATEGIES UNDER EVALUATION: Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This authority is intended for military construction projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. Currently, the Government has advanced the design to 35% and has the capability to progress to a full design. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing Construction Management at Risk (CM@Risk) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The CM@Risk Course of Action (10 U.S.C. � 2808a): This Course of Action utilizes the 10 U.S.C. � 2808a OT authority to execute a construction project where the design is at 35% completion. Phase 1 Preconstruction: The builder is hired during Phase 1 to act as an expert consultant, helping the Designer of Record (DOR) push the design from 35% to 100% using real-time market data and MII (MCACES 2nd Generation) cost comparisons. Phase 2 Construction: Once the design hits 100% and the MII estimate validates the open-book pricing, the agreement transitions to Phase 2, where the builder goes "At-Risk" to construct the facility under a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). The DOR retains design liability, but the contractor drives constructability and assumes responsibility for layout, schedule, and trade coordination. The CM@Risk Pricing Structure: Preconstruction Services Fee: A small, fixed-price or time-and-materials amount paid to the contractor strictly to fund their time spent helping the Architect Engineer (A/E) finalize the 35% design into a 100% design. The Target Fee: The contractor�s transparent profit margin for managing the actual construction, bid competitively upfront. The GMP: The absolute ceiling for the construction phase (Validated Direct Costs + Target Fee + Shared Contingency). PHASED EXECUTION PLAN Phase 1: Preconstruction Services Agreement (CM@Risk Advisory) Solicitation (White Papers): The Solicitation would likely include the 35% design. The Deliverable is anticipated to be a concise 5-10 page White Paper. Evaluation Criteria will likely include Corporate capability and experience with collaborative project delivery methods ( including CM@Risk, Progressive Design-Build (PDB) and/or Design-Build to Budget (DBtB)) under an OT framework; preconstruction approach (how the firm plans to collaborate with the Government's A/E to close the remaining 65% design gap, identify value-engineering opportunities, and mitigate supply-chain risks); proposed Target Fee (for construction) and Preconstruction Services Fee. The Pitch Meeting (Oral Presentations): A 90-minute pitch where the contractor must bring their Project Manager, Site Superintendent, and their Preconstruction Manager. The Government team assesses how well the contractor's team will integrate with the A/E during the critical final design push. The OT is initially awarded and funded only for the Preconstruction Services Fee. Design Finalization (Bridging the 65% Gap): The contractor�s Preconstruction team sits with the Government and the DOR. Because the design is not locked, they can actively change it. They perform value engineering, finalize equipment selections, and ensure the drawings are 100% constructible. title: Guatemala – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Asistencia Técnica para la implementación de la Agenda de inversiones Global Gateway en Guatemala – Global Gateway Facility Guatemala
description: En 2021, la Comisión Europea lanzó la estrategia de inversiones Global Gateway, que tiene como objetivo fomentar inversiones de gran calibre en infraestructura verde y digital en los países socios, con soluciones innovadoras y de calidad, creando al mismo tiempo valor añadido local y promoviendo el crecimiento económico, el empleo y la cohesión social. Durante la III Cumbre UE-CELAC, celebrada en julio de 2023, los dirigentes de ambas regiones reafirmaron su compromiso de reforzar la asociación birregional, reconociendo la importancia de la Agenda de Inversiones Global Gateway. Dicho compromiso fue renovado durante la IV Cumbre UE-CELAC celebrada en noviembre de 2025. El objetivo general de esta acción es contribuir a la implementación de inversiones sostenibles y transformadoras en los sectores de transición verde y digital en Guatemala, donde haya un interés común europeo y de la agenda de desarrollo de Guatemala, y ello en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway, asegurando su alineación con las prioridades estratégicas del país y fomentando un desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible. La Asistencia Técnica contribuirá a: mejorar la alineación, coordinación y monitoreo de las iniciativas implementadas en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway en Guatemala; promover un marco regulatorio e institucional que favorezca la inversión sostenible en los sectores prioritarios de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway; impulsar proyectos de inversión sostenibles, transformadores y sensibles a la igualdad de género y a las buenas prácticas internacionales en materia de derechos y protección del medioambiente en los sectores prioritarios y a posicionar los intereses del sector privado europeo en el marco de la Agenda de Inversión Global Gateway para Guatemala. Sin excluir otras potenciales áreas de trabajo prioritarias para la UE y Guatemala, y reconociendo la flexibilidad dinámica de la estrategia Global Gateway, las áreas prioritarias para Guatemala actualmente incluyen transición verde (transporte sostenible, energía renovable e integración eléctrica regional, economía circular, gestión sostenible de recursos naturales y residuos) y transición digital (conectividad, gobernanza digital, ciberseguridad, innovación digital, observación de la Tierra, inteligencia artificial).

description: The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a Cabinet-level executive branch department of the Federal Government whose workforce is comprised of approximately 650,000 clinical and non-clinical personnel (of which approximately 450,000 are employees) charged with providing lifelong healthcare services to eligible military veterans at the 1,380 health care facilities, including 170 VA medical centers and 1,193 outpatient sites located throughout the country. Non-healthcare benefits include disability compensation, vocational rehabilitation, education assistance, home loans, and life insurance. The VA also provides burial and memorial benefits to eligible veterans and family members at the 157 VA managed or 125 VA grant-funded cemeteries. VA employs a highly skilled and multi-faceted workforce aligned with its mission, program, and operational needs. Workforce Development is one of the key factors to recruiting and retaining a high-performing workforce. VA employs individuals at every competency and skill level whether they are new to the workforce or experts in their occupation. That said, VA workforce needs differ at every career stage. VA Federal personnel are encouraged annually to complete My Development Plans (MDP). They work with supervisors to determine short and long- term career goals as well as short-term training needs. Training needs are then documented on the MDP. The VA�s Leadership Development Framework (LDF) is based on the Federal-wide United States Office of Personnel Management Executive Core Qualifications. By using the VA LDF, VA personnel will be better able to assess their leadership capabilities for developmental purposes and to support the Department�s workforce, talent development, and succession planning efforts. Certain VA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices require its workforce to complete technical competency assessments and leadership competency assessments for non-supervisory positions. VA personnel will complete leadership and technical competency assessments through the Department�s Talent Management System (TMS) 2.0 or Learning Management system of record (LMS). VA personnel must also meet certain training requirements throughout the year. These requirements may be prescribed as Federal Mandatory Training such as No Fear Act, Information Security Awareness, Occupational Health, and Safety, or Telework. Some personnel must complete training required by their occupation or role such as Cyber security role-based training. VA personnel access most of their training through Talent Management System TMS 2.0. This platform provides a common LMS and learning content services that enable VA to maximize the return on taxpayer investment. TMS 2.0 has a robust and secure environment to accommodate approximately 450,000 end users, ~12,000 administrators and over 500 unique domains. TMS 2.0 is the Department-wide system for managing training records and activities at VA. The purpose of this contract is to acquire eContent, Digital Books, Professional Development Training and Support Services to meet the training requirement of VA.

description: IDA Ireland is seeking to establish of a Single Party Framework for the Design, Delivery and Management of IDA Ireland’s Property Management System on the Salesforce platform. Justification for the maximum 7 years Framework length - The successful candidate may be required to undertake potentially significant upfront time investment in further discovery, detailed solution design, data migration, configuration, testing, integration and organisational change activities. In its current off-the-shelf form, a Salesforce solution is not capable of meeting all of IDA Property’s requirements without tailoring and multiple integration points with third party systems. This will be delivered through controlled configuration and integration activities that will may require extended timescales. The option of the extension of the framework to a maximum of 7 years will allow the IDA (provided that the successful tenderer has performed in a satisfactory manner) to obtain the benefit of the framework support as envisaged in the event of a prolonged implementation period.

title: Elevator Maintenance, Testing, Inspection, and Repair Services at Naval Air Station Meridian, MS
description: The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, supplies, equipment, tools, and transportation required for maintaining six elevators, in a continuously safe, reliable, and satisfactory operating condition and to perform all inspections and testing as required. Five (5) elevators are located at Naval Air Station Meridian, MS, and one (1) elevator is located at Outlying Joe Williams Field in Kemper County, MS. The Contractor will provide recurring monthly services, periodic testing, and non-recurring on-demand repair services to the Government in exchange for compensation. title: Brand Name Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS)
description: 8 September 2026 Update Solicitation/Draft contract change in Statement of Work Combined Synopsis/Solicitation: Brand Name Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) Solicitation Number: FA8601-26-Q-0074 Notice Type: Special Notice (RFQ) Issuing Office: AFLCMC/PZIBA Posted Date: 9 September 2026 Response Date: 25 September 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT Set-Aside: N/A Product Service Code: 6630 NAICS Code: 334516 Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 Employees Description The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC/PZIBA), on behalf of the Department of the Air Force at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, intends to award a Brand Name Only, firm-fixed-price contract for an Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS). This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products prepared in accordance with Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; offers are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses in effect through the RFO, effective 17 April 2026, and the Revolutionary Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (RDFARS) as of the date of issuance. The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price contract for an Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) in accordance with the attached Statement of Work (SOW), dated 1 September 2026, on a Lowest Price Technically Acceptable basis. The Schedule of Supplies, place of performance, delivery information, and the full list of applicable provisions and clauses are set forth in the attached SF 1449 and solicitation. Award is subject to the availability of funds. The requirement is for all supplies, labor, and services necessary to procure a new High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS). This is a follow-on acquisition requiring the new HPLC-MS to be fully compatible and interchangeable with the agency�s existing Agilent equipment and software. The Government�s market research indicates that Agilent products use proprietary MassHunter software for instrument control and data analysis, and no other manufacturer produces a compatible system that meets the Government�s essential need for a single, integrated platform while avoiding the cost of new training and method redevelopment. The approved Brand Name Justification is attached to this posting. Submission Instructions Submission Deadline: 25 September 2026, 11:00 a.m. EDT Required Email Subject Line: FA8601-26-Q-0074, Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) Offerors shall submit proposals by email to all of the following points of contact: Candice Snow candice.snow@us.af.mil Alejandro Quiles alejandro.quiles_sanchez.1@us.af.mil Brian Algeo brian.algeo.1@us.af.mil Format: Submit a single email not exceeding 5 MB. Attachments must be in PDF, DOCX, or XLSX format. Compressed files, including ZIP files, are not permitted. Confirmation: A receipt confirmation will be sent within 24 hours. If confirmation is not received, contact all three points of contact listed above. Proposal Content Requirements Proposals shall consist of a Technical Proposal and a Price Proposal and shall provide sufficient detail to demonstrate compliance with the SOW. Offerors shall not merely restate Government requirements. Each proposal shall include: Company name, address, SAM Unique Entity ID, CAGE Code, and TIN. Point-of-contact name, telephone number, and email address. Proposal number, proposal date, and proposal validity period. Technical description, manuals, data sheets, or product literature demonstrating compliance with each SOW requirement. A complete price schedule matching the CLIN structure provided in the solicitation. Total Evaluated Price. Completed offeror representations and certifications, including country-of-origin information for the offered end product and applicable components. Itemized firm-fixed-price information with extended totals. Pricing shall include shipping, unloading, and final setup at AFIT Building 644, Room L139. Payment terms shall be Net 30. Progress payments are not authorized. Confirmation that the offeror is Agilent or an authorized Agilent reseller. If submitting an offer as an authorized reseller, the offeror shall provide a manufacturer authorization letter verifying authorization to sell the offered system to the Government. Technical description of the items offered sufficient to verify part-number accuracy and compliance with the SOW. Key Information Requirement: Agilent High-Performance Liquid Chromatograph-Mass Spectrometer (HPLC-MS) in accordance with the SOW dated 1 September 2026. Contract Type: Firm-Fixed Price. Period of Performance: Six months after contract award. Delivery: Delivery, installation, unloading, storage, and final setup shall occur at the Air Force Institute of Technology, Building 644, Room L139, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification In accordance with RDFARS 252.204-7021, this acquisition requires Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) Level 1 for Federal Contract Information only. Offerors must have a current CMMC Level 1, or higher, self-assessment recorded in the Supplier Performance Risk System at the time of award. Waivers, grace periods, and Plans of Action and Milestones are not permitted. Buy American Act and Qualifying-Country Products This acquisition is subject to the Buy American Act and the qualifying-country-product requirements set forth in the SOW. In accordance with the SOW, all products proposed or delivered shall be domestic end products or qualifying-country end products, as applicable. Offerors shall identify the country of origin for the offered end product and applicable components in the required representations and certifications. The offered HPLC-MS system must be made and assembled in the United States of America in accordance with the SOW. Basis for Award Award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal: Conforms to this combined synopsis/solicitation; Receives an �Acceptable� rating for Technical Capability, as demonstrated by compliance with all SOW requirements, domestic assembly, and authorized Agilent sourcing credentials; and Contains the lowest Total Evaluated Price determined fair, reasonable, and not unbalanced. Past Performance and Responsibility Before award, the Contracting Officer will perform a responsibility determination under RFO Part 9, including review of the offeror�s record in the Contractor Performance Assessment Reporting System and the Supplier Performance Risk System. Adverse findings may render an offeror non-responsible. The Government reserves the right to award without discussions or to make no award. Important Notices SAM Registration: Offerors must maintain an active registration in the System for Award Management for the life of the contract. description: REPAIR ROOF Federal Prison Camp HVAC, Plumb and Comm. Shop at FCC Terre Haute. This is a Sources Sought Notice. This notice is issued for market research purposes only. The FBOP is seeking small business contractors for this project. Your business size metrics information entered in your SAM registration must be less than or equal to the small business size standard specified above to qualify as a small business. Subcontracts (if applicable/necessary) are the responsibility of the Prime contractor. The FBOP has no privity of contract with subcontractors. Interested parties are also requested to complete the attached Market Research Questionnaire and return the completed document to rmoothery@bop.gov. no later than September 25, 2026 by 11am. Correspondence will be by email only. Please do not call. A pre-construction site visit will be scheduled at a later date, followed by a combined synopsis / solicitation. Interested parties must submit to a criminal background check. The combined synopsis/solicitation of the proposed contract action will include further instructions for responding to this opportunity. Interested bidders are advised to continuously monitor www.sam.gov for all future updates.

title: Pakistan NDC 3.0 Delivery Coordination Mechanism (Federal-Provincial Coordination and Tracking)
description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the Government of Pakistan. Pakistan has committed to reducing projected greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2035 through its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) 3.0. Delivering this target will depend heavily on action at the provincial level, where responsibility for many climate-relevant sectors rests. While the Government of Pakistan has established new coordination arrangements through the National Climate Finance Strategy (NCFS), challenges remain around federal-provincial coordination, implementation tracking, climate finance visibility, and reporting progress against national climate commitments. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance to support the Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination (MoCC&EC), the Pakistan Climate Change Authority (PCCA), and provincial governments to establish and operationalise a practical federal-provincial coordination and tracking mechanism for NDC 3.0 implementation. The project will strengthen institutional coordination, improve monitoring and reporting of climate actions and investments, build government capacity, and support the mobilisation of climate finance. The intervention will also integrate Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) considerations to promote more inclusive climate governance and decision-making. Key outputs are expected to include a federal-provincial NDC coordination framework, a standardised NDC tracking and reporting framework, an interoperability pilot connecting existing government climate and public-sector data systems, operational support for a Tactical Climate Coordination Forum, and a sustainability and scale-up roadmap. The project aims to strengthen Pakistan's ability to implement and report on its climate commitments, improve evidence-based decision-making, enhance transparency and accountability, and create a stronger foundation for attracting climate finance and accelerating NDC delivery across provinces and sectors. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk.

QUESTIONS Questions regarding this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to the Contracting Officer at Chaunda.Stewart@hhs.gov no later than September 16, 2026 at 5:00pm Eastern Time (ET). No faxes or phone calls please. Questions received after this deadline will not receive a response. PROPOSALS The proposals must be submitted no later than September 25, 2026 at 12:00 pm Eastern Time (ET). The offeror shall submit four (4) separate volumes in electronic versions in portable document format (PDF) format of the technical proposal (Volume I), the business/cost proposals (Volume II), past performance (Volume III) and technical proposal demo of web portal (Volume IV) to the Government. Offerors shall acknowledge receipt of all amendments in accordance with the instructions provided in each amendment. Any amendment to this solicitation will be posted to SAM.gov. NAICS The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition: NAICS Code (Primary): 423450 � Medical, Dental, and Hospital Equipment and Supplies Merchant Wholesalers NAICS Code (Secondary): 424210 � Drugs and Druggists� Sundries Merchant Wholesalers PURPOSE The purpose of this contract is to acquire medications, vaccines and medical supplies (MVMS) for Federal Occupational Health (FOH) locations through a nationwide, contractor managed web-based ordering portal to support the Program Support Center under the Department of Health and Human Services. This contract aims to consolidate operations, offering a more convenient, reliable and cost-effective approach to MVMS procurement. Services range from core occupational health and safety programs to structured clinical, wellness, behavioral health, and environmental health solutions. FOH retains sole responsibility for consulting with customer agencies, while the contractor facilitates delivery of services outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) as well as the solicitation found in the attachments section. FOH sets the standard for promoting a culture of health and safety across the federal workforce. Program effectiveness depends on the expertise and performance of contractor-managed operations, including procurement of Medications, Vaccines and Medical Supplies (MVMS). Historically, FOH has sourced MVMS from multiple vendors, including the Program Support Center�s fulfillment center. This contract will consolidate MVMS procurement into a more efficient, reliable, and cost-effective model; reduce reliance on government purchase cards and unstable supply chains; and strengthen FOH oversight of procurement activities. title: Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) is soliciting innovative proposals in the following technical area: physics and nonlinear control of inertial measurement units (IMUs) appropriate for tactical and unmanned missions. The Precision Inertial Navigation & Positioning On an Integrated Tesseract (PINPOINT) program will challenge the research community to overcome the decade-long performance plateau of micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) IMUs by exploring revolutionary sensor architectures that operate in highly nonlinear regimes. DARPA is soliciting proposals for the research and development of novel inertial sensors based on physics such as, but not limited to, electromagnetically levitated proof masses, non-linear resonators, and high-velocity tethered microsystems. A central theme of this program is the tight co-design of the physical sensor package with advanced, real-time adaptive control systems necessary to stabilize and harness these complex dynamics. Performers should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice.

title: Measurement of Benzene Emissions from Gasoline Dispensing Facilities
description: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC)’s mandate includes the preservation and enhancement of the quality of the natural environment, including water, air and soil quality. Accordingly, ECCC works in conjunction with Health Canada (HC) and other departments to understand the risks posed by the release of toxic substances, then develop policy as needed to effectively manage these releases. Benzene is recognized as a human carcinogen by HC (Canada 1993) and the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) (IARC 2018), among other international agencies. In addition, short-term exposure (over hours to days) is associated with hematotoxicity, including during fetal development. Benzene is a constituent of gasoline and, as a volatile organic compound (VOC), readily evaporates and is released into the atmosphere from gasoline service stations. Exposure to benzene through inhalation of emissions from these facilities may pose unacceptable risks to human health for members of the general population residing in the vicinity of gasoline stations. ECCC wishes to study benzene concentrations in the air in the vicinity of gasoline stations Canada, ideally in the Ottawa-Gatineau area, to improve understanding of the human health implications of benzene emissions from these facilities and validate the efficacy of emissions control equipment in cases where it is installed. The contractor will contribute to this objective by measuring ambient concentrations of benzene and, where feasible, other VOCs or total VOCs at gasoline stations before, during, and after gasoline deliveries, in accordance with the parameters set out in this Statement of Work. The Contractor must perform and complete the Work within the period commencing upon notification of acceptance of the offer and ending no later than March 31, 2027. For additional information, interested suppliers should contact Helena Lee at; Helena.Lee@ec.gc.ca.

buyer: The Common Services Agency (more commonly known as Public Services Delivery Scotland) (PSD Scotland)
title: Service Integration and Management System (SIAM)
description: PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for the transition, stabilisation and continued delivery of selected national digital services supporting health and care across Scotland. The successful supplier will act as prime contractor and provide a single point of accountability for end-to-end service delivery, integration and performance. The supplier will also be responsible for the management of any subcontractors and dependencies with other providers and Authority teams. The initial priority will be to maintain continuity and stabilise these business-critical services as they transition away from the existing National IT Contract, while establishing a strong foundation for subsequent improvement and modernisation.

title: Flood Bank Realignment
description: This collaborative project with SBAG address recurring concerns over beaver burrowing and floodbank breaches on high-value farmland along the River Isla, a major tributary of the River Tay (SAC). By realigning a floodbank and creating a wider more natural river corridor with willow buffer strip we intend to increase bank resilience, reduce beaver impacts and enhance biodiversity. Two participating agricultural landowners will trial setback embankments and habitat features including beaver mounds to encourage coexistence. The approach integrates agricultural resilience with river naturalisation, monitored by the river Restoration Centre and Beaver Trust to inform future coexistence strategies to promote biodiversity.

title: Program Manager Counterproliferation (PMCP) Service Support
description: **UPDATE AS OF 09 SEPTEMBER 2026** The purpose of this update is to notify industry that the final Request for Proposal (RFP) is scheduled for release the week of 21 September 2026, and that the Government has completed responses to all questions received during the Draft RFP phase. Due to Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) handling restrictions, the Q&A document will not be posted publicly and must be requested through formal access controls. To obtain access to the restricted Draft RFP Q&A document, interested parties must request access through SAM.gov. Prior to granting access, the government will verify that the contractor maintains a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment score of 110 posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS). Once the Government confirms a vendor can receive and safeguard CUI, the Draft RFP Q&A document will be available for review in SAM.gov. Additionally, interested parties are hereby notified that the final RFP and all associated solicitation documentation will be issued, managed, and submitted exclusively through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Solicitation Module. To facilitate timely access and ensure vendors are fully prepared to submit proposals, PIEE registration and user access instructions are attached to this notice. Vendors are strongly encouraged to verify account readiness and establish appropriate system roles in advance of the RFP release. Further, all interested vendors must submit a new executed Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) to receive the final RFP. NDAs previously executed during the Draft RFP phase will not satisfy this requirement. The final RFP NDA is attached to this notice, and vendors are encouraged to execute and submit their NDAs in advance of the Government�s formal solicitation release scheduled for the week of 21 September. All signed NDAs shall be submitted via email to SOCOM.PMCP.SPTSVC.RFP.SHDMBX@socom.mil. The following link is provided to access the PIEE solicitation module training: https://pieetraining.eb.mil/wbt/xhtml/wbt/sol/index.xhtml This notification includes three attachments: 1. PMCP-SS_RFP_NDA 2. PIEE_Solicitation_Module_Vendor_Access_Instructions 3. PMCPSS Draft RFP Q&A **UPDATE AS OF 25 AUGUST 2026** The purpose of this update is to notify industry that the final Request for Proposal (RFP) is scheduled for release on September 9, 2026. Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for H9240226RE003, Program Manager Counterproliferation (PMCP) Service Support Contract The Special Operations Forces Acquisition, Technology and Logistics (SOF AT&L) core mission is to provide rapid and focused acquisition, technology, and logistics support to SOF Warfighters. Under SOF AT&L, the Program Manager for Counterproliferation (PMCP) is chartered with the procurement, development, testing, training, fielding, and sustainment of technologies in support of Electronic Warfare (EW), advanced Counter Improvised Explosive Device (C-IED) operations and Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) for improvised explosive device threats and Counter-Unmanned System (C-UxS) threats. Interested industry partners are encouraged to submit a request, including company name and CAGE code to the below Points of Contact (POCs). This information will be used to verify in the System for Award management (SAM) and the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) that the offeror can receive CUI documents. After successful verification, the documents will be provided for review and submission of questions, comments, or suggestions. We are particularly interested in feedback regarding the clarity of evaluation criteria, pricing structure, and feasibility of the past performance relevancy measures. Please submit your feedback using the RFP Q&A Template provided with this RFP Letter to the POCs listed below no later than 1300 hours ET on 15 June 2026.

title: FSC Meridian Fire Reporting & Control Systems, NAS Meridian
description: Naval Air Station Meridian is located in east-central Mississippi, near Meridian, Mississippi in Lauderdale and Kemper counties. Approximately 20 miles northeast of the city of Meridian between State Highways 39 and 45. NAS Meridian hosts Training Air Wing One (TRAWING-1). The installation serves as a premier jet flight-training base, supporting Training Squadron 7 (VT-7) and Training Squadron 9 (VT-9). The air station trains hundreds of Navy and Marine Corps student aviators utilizing the T-45C Goshawk jet trainer. There are outlying fields used for student training. All maintenance and repair shall be performed by personnel trained and certified by the OEM. Personnel inspecting, witnessing tests, preparing reports, and issuing certificates for boilers and UPVs must be qualified per UFC 3-430-07. Personnel inspecting, certifying, and making recommendations for corrective action for backflow preventers shall be certified per UG-2029-ENV. Personnel working on fire protection systems must be certified per UFC 3-601-02 and shall be licensed in the state of Mississippi, as applicable. Fire Protection services shall be managed by a qualified individual who is NICET level III certified in fire alarm or NICET level III certified in special hazards systems. Personnel working on fire protection systems shall be certified in accordance with the requirements below: Fire Alarm Systems: ? Fire Alarm: NICET Level II certification in Fire Alarm Systems. ? Detection and releasing systems for Special Hazard Systems such as those found in aircraft hangars and computer server rooms: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems Water Based Suppression Systems: ? Wet Pipe and Dry Pipe Sprinklers: NICET Level II certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. ? Pre-Action, Deluge, Foam and Antifreeze Systems: NICET Level III certification in Inspection and Testing of Water Based Systems. Special Hazard Systems: ? Clean Agent, CO2 and Combination Detection/Releasing Systems: NICET Level II certification in Special Hazard Systems. Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems: ? NICET Level II certification in Special Hazards Suppression Systems or certified by ICC/NAFED in Pre-Engineered Kitchen Fire Extinguishing Systems. The service technician shall have the applicable manufacturer�s design, installation, and maintenance manual and service bulletins. Less qualified personnel may assist NICET Levels II and III certified personnel in the execution of inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task. At no time shall less qualified personnel be allowed to execute inspection, testing, maintenance and repair task without a qualified NICET Level II or III. The Contractor shall also perform maintenance on NAS Meridian Water Plant SCADA system to ensure proper operation, to minimize breakdowns, and to maximize useful life.The Contractor shall conduct annual testing, calibration and adjustment of the system form the control point to the terminations at the monitoring devices, individual well houses, chemical mixers or injectors, valves and motor controllers. The performance of this contract requires maintenance, monitoring, programming, and integration services on specific proprietary control systems, Life Safety systems, and Industrial Control Systems (ICS). These include, but are not limited to, Johnson Controls, Simplex, Monaco, and Honeywell systems, as well as SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) water control systems. Interested sources must demonstrate existing technical competency, direct access to necessary proprietary software/firmware/tools, and current Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) authorization, certifications, or formal partnership agreements required to service, modify, and maintain these proprietary systems without voiding warranties or compromising system integrity. Respondents should be prepared to provide: (1) Proof of active OEM authorization/certification or licensed integrator status for the listed proprietary systems; (2) Evidence of personnel holding relevant manufacturer credentials/certifications (e.g., NICET II+ for fire alarm systems, certified ICS/PLC programmers for plant control); and (3) A brief summary of past performance involving identical or similar proprietary systems within an operational environment.

title: FCC BUTNER - WATER CHEMICAL TESTING AND CONSULTATION SERVICES
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for the Water Chemical Testing and Consultation Services for the Federal Correctional Complex Butner, prepared in accordance with FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The Federal Bureau of Prisons (FBOP), Field Acquisition Office (FAO), intends to award an indefinite deliver/requirements type contract with firm-fixed unit pricing. The award will be based on price and past performance. The contract periods for the service will consist of a base year with four, 12-month option years, at the unilateral discretion of the Government. Solicitation number 15BGCS26Q10600001 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) to any interested party (unrestricted procurement. The North American Industrial Classification (NAICS) code is 325998 with a small business size standard of 650 employees. The solicitation document (RFQ), located in the Attachments/Links section, contains the Statement of Work (SOW), of which provides a detailed description of the requirement(s) of the items to be acquired, a list of line-item number(s) and items, quantities and units of measure (including option(s), if applicable). Quotes shall be submitted, on or before the solicitation deadline Specified in Block 8 of the Standard Form 1449, via email, to Justin Wray at jwray@bop.gov. Failure to provide all quotation requirements on most up to date RFQ may result in your quote being eliminated from consideration for award. Hard copies of the solicitation will not be available. The website provides all downloading instructions to obtain a copy of the solicitation. All contractors doing business with the Federal Government are advised that this future solicitation includes the provision at FAR 52.204-7, System for Award Management (SAM); of this provision requires all contractors doing business with the federal government to be registered in the SAM database at www.sam.gov. Contractors shall include their Unique Entity Identification Number (UEI) number in their offers. The Contracting Officer will verify registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to award by entering the potential awardees UEI number into the SAM database. If you have already sent your RFIs to the POCs you do not have to resubmit them. 4 August 2026: Please see the attached RFP (FA8137-26-R-0040) and all attachments. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- THIS POSTING WILL SATISFY THE REQUIREMENT OF RFO 5.101, Presolicitation Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) for General Construction Services will accomplish a broad range of sustainment, maintenance, repair, alteration/renovation, and minor construction projects affecting real property facilities at Tinker Air Force Base, Oklahoma. The work performed will be complex in nature, require multiple construction trades, and may require engineering design performed by credentialed professionals. Project execution methods will fall into one of the following classifications. The execution method will be defined in the project documents for each Task Order (TO) under this Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quanity (IDIQ) contract. Design Build will include the Contractor providing both the design and construction services for a project; during the Design-Build process, final design solutions are provided by the Contractor, not the Government. The Government will provide a Statement of Work (SOW), drawings, and other preliminary documents to establish requirements from the work to be completed. These documents will be equivalent to a schematic 15% or greater design. When awarded the TO for the project, the Contractor will complete the design to the 100% level to include drawings, specifications, design analysis/narrative, and other documentation as required by the Government. Construction with Limited Design method will include the Government providing the design and the Contractor will further develop portions as required and will provide construction services for the project. This method will be used for non-complex or repetitive work types of projects where design cost and effort is not warranted. The Government will provide the SOW, drawings, and other documents as necessary to establish requirements to complete the project. These documents will be equivalent to a design submittal 35% to 65%. When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. When awarded the TO the Contractor shall commence with construction in accordance with the design and contract requirements. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 236210, Industrial Building Construction with a small business size standard of $45 million. The MACC will be executed for one base period of five (5) years with one option period of five (5) years. The Government will negotiate equitable adjustments resulting from change orders in the shortest practicable time. Approximately 120 days are required to definitize equitable adjustments associated with change orders for construction. The definitization of an equitable adjustment begins when the contracting officer receives an adequate change order definitization proposal and ends when the contracting officer executes a contractual action to definitize the change order. title: Notice Of Intent to Sole Source - Thermo Fisher Scientific Asheville LLC - Centrifuge Calibration
description: The purpose of this acquisition is to have Health Effects Laboratory Division (HELD) centrifuges undergo preventative maintenance and calibration. Regular calibration of centrifuges is essential because it ensures that rotational speed, temperature control (when applicable), and timing functions remain accurate, which directly affects the reliability and reproducibility of experimental results. The vendor shall perform visual and functional checks for rotor condition, imbalance indicators, lid locks, refrigeration performance (where applicable), and overall mechanical integrity. Key parameters will be calibrated according to International Standard Organization (ISO) 17025 standards.

It is not a request for quotes nor does it obligate the government in any way. The Government will not reimburse the respondents for any costs associated with the information submitted in response to this request. Additionally, this RFI notice does not guarantee that the government will issue a request for quotes or award a contract for supplies or services. The National Weather Service (NWS), Ocean Prediction Center (OPC), U.S. National Ice Center (USNIC) has a need for georeferenced GeoTIFFs of global coverage in accessible electronic format 24/7/365 and with the capability of near-real-time latency. SAR imagery�s benefits remain helpful to the persistence of USNIC�s operational programs of earth surface observation in the poor weather or illumination conditions of the polar latitudes. Near-real-time latency is considered to be the capability of delivering images deemed to be time critical to USNIC no more than approximately four (4) hours from time of satellite acquisition. Delivery beyond this period prohibits the USNIC from fulfilling an operational requirement to produce timely products and respond to tactical needs. **See attached documents for information being requested and further details**

title: Collaborative Testing Services (CTS) Proficiency Testing Supplies
description: This notice announces the intent by the Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA) Fort Detrick, Maryland, 21702, to award a sole source Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Contract to Collaborative Testing Services (CTS) under the statutory authority 12.102(a). The contract is for the purchase of Scheduled proficiency tests shipped at specified dates (vendor dependent) to include testing materials (bloodstains, dried body fluid stains, dried saliva samples) for the Armed Forces Medical Examiner System (AFMES), Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFDIL). Collaborative Testing Services, LLC (CTS) is the only responsible source capable of providing the highly specialized proficiency testing supplies and services required to maintain the accreditation and operational integrity of the Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory (AFMES/AFDIL). While four proficiency testing providers are recognized by laboratory accrediting bodies�Collaborative Testing Services, Bode Cellmark Forensics, College of American Pathologists (CAP), and Serological Research Institute (SERI)�comprehensive market research and technical evaluation confirm that only CTS satisfies the agency�s minimum operational, throughput, and scientific requirements. The remaining three providers present critical technical deficiencies that make them unsuitable for AFDIL�s casework requirements: Bode Cellmark Forensics offers infrequent testing schedules that cannot support AFDIL�s staffing capacity or rolling test intervals; SERI imposes compressed completion windows that are incompatible with the extended processing times required by AFDIL�s advanced testing technologies; and CAP utilizes a manual, scan-based submission process that introduces an unacceptable risk of data transcription errors. In contrast, CTS uniquely provides the validated test substrates, electronic reporting infrastructure, and staggered distribution schedules necessary to efficiently test personnel on a continuous basis without disrupting critical forensic operations. Procuring these tests from any other source would jeopardize compliance with time-sensitive accreditation standards, compromise the validity of future casework, and introduce substantial risks to the laboratory's mission. CTS is the sole provider that meets all required sample matrices, capacity requirements, and distribution intervals. Delivery Date: 01 November 2026 The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 334516 and the size standard is 1,250 Employees. Any other firms desiring consideration must fully identify their interest in and capability to provide these services to the individual listed below. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written responses are received by the expiration date listed in this notice, which reflects at least fifteen (15) days after the publication of this notice, the award will be issued as sole source. All questions and responses concerning this notice shall be emailed to Mr. Christopher L. Cook at christopher.l.cook68.civ@health.mil.

When awarded the TO the Contractor will complete any additional design efforts required by the project and produce a set of working documents for use during construction. Construction only method will include the Government providing 100% design package, including the SOW, drawings, specification, and any other documents as necessary to establish requirements for the work to be accomplished. The Contractor is required to furnish all materials, labor, plant, tools, transportation, equipment, testing services, quality control, and incidentals necessary to provide a complete useable end product as specified in the TO/project documents. title: P110 CAPE CANAVERAL RAILHEAD AND TRANSFER FACILITIES AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER, FLORIDA
description: This is a request for information/market survey. This is not a request for proposal, request for quote, or an invitation for bid. There will be no solicitation, specification, or drawings available at this time. Naval Facilities Engineering System Command (NAVFAC) Southeast is soliciting comments from the public addressing the potential use of Project Labor Agreements (PLA) for the following construction project. The construction project involves constructing railroad trackage to connect and facilitate the transfer from commercial rail to the on-base processing facility at Cape Canaveral. Constructs a low-rise open air standing seam-metal roofed canopy on a reinforced shallow foundation with wide-flange beams and columns and continuous footings for a Submarine Launched Ballistic Missile Processing Facility (Motor Transfer Facility). Functions include receiving and shipping missile motors, components and Active Inert Missiles (AIMS) which require superflat floors for air pallet operations. The roof structure will include sloped, uninsulated metal roof panels on steel joists. Project will be design-bid-build. NAICS Code: 237990. The magnitude of construction is anticipated to be $25,000,000 � $100,000,000. General period of performance is anticipated to be approximately 527 calendar days. A PLA is defined as a pre-hire collective bargaining agreement with one or more labor organizations that establishes the terms and conditions of employment for a specific construction project and is an agreement as described in 29 U.S.C. 158 (f). Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) policy states: Executive Order (E.O.) 14063, Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects, requires agencies to use PLAs in large-scale construction projects (defined as a construction projects with a total estimated cost at or above $35M) to promote economy and efficiency in the administration and completion of Federal construction projects. When awarding a contract in connection with a large-scale construction project, agencies shall require use of a PLA for contractors and subcontractors engaged in construction on the project, unless an exception(s) at FAR 22.504(d) applies. Reference is made to: FAR Subpart 22.5 Use of Project Labor Agreements for Federal Construction Projects; provision, FAR 52.222-33 Notice of Requirement for Project Labor Agreement; and to clause, FAR 52.222-34 Project Labor Agreement. In consideration of the above factors, and any others which may be deemed appropriate, the public is invited to provide responses on the use of a PLA for this construction project utilizing the attached questionnaire. In light of recent court decisions on PLAs, the Government is seeking additional information on the use of PLAs for this project. This survey is for planning purposes only and shall not be construed as an obligation on the part of the Government. The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this market survey or otherwise pay for the requested information. The Government will not provide a debriefing on the results of this survey. All information will be held in a confidential manner and will only be used for the purposes intended. (See question #4) Responses shall be submitted on the attached questionnaire via email to Deborah Torrence, deborah.d.torrence2.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 2:00 PM ET on September 25, 2026.

title: Blanket Purchase Agreement - Sample Testing
description: The requirement is for the establishment of single Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPA) for the testing of metal coupons to aid the QA process of the components with which these coupons are associated. The Contractor�s laboratory facility must be validated by the USACE Materials Testing Center (MTC) along with maintain ISO/IEC 17025 certification and remain validated throughout the life of this agreement. Project Background The Contractor shall receive, test mechanical and/or chemical characteristics, and submit reports of coupon materials to aid the QA process of the associated components supplied to the Government via other ongoing contract efforts. The coupons will be shipped directly to the Contractor, many of which will likely come from international locations. The Contractor will not be responsible for shipping or duty costs to receive coupons. The coupon materials that may be tested include but may not be limited to ASTM A743 Grade CA6NM and Grade CF3, ASTM A27 Grade 70-40, ASTM A148 Grade 80-40, ASTM A216 Grade WCC, and ASTM A516 Grade 60. The tests that may be required include chemical analysis according to ASTM A751, carbon combustion according to ASTM E1019-18, tensile tests (yield strength, tensile strength, elongation, and reduction of area) according to ASTM A370, hardness tests according to ASTM A370, and Charpy v-notch impact tests according to ASTM A370. The range of tests completed for a given coupon will depend on the material and component with which it is associated. There may be provisions for optional storage of coupons, both tested and untested. Disposal of excess coupons may be considered at no additional cost to the Government.

title: BEYOND Phase 2
description: Amendment 0001 is hereby issued to extend the proposal due date of the SIR to September 25, 2026 at 3:00pm ET. No other changes result from Amendment 0001. __________________________________________________ This is the Screening Information Request (SIR) 697DCK-26-R-00423 for the BEYOND Phase 2 Selection. This procurement is in support of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Unmanned Aircraft Systems and Advanced Air Mobility Integration Office (AUS). The FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (P.L.118-63) Section 920 allows for the expansion of the BEYOND program. The FAA will implement a BEYOND Phase 2 competitive selection process, through this SIR. This competitive selection process is not a procurement or acquisition under the FAA Acquisition Management System. The FAA did not develop any acquisition requirements for this competitive selection process, and the process will not result in the award of a procurement contract. Consistent with the FAA Administrator�s authorities under 49 U.S.C. �106(l) and (m), this process will result in the award of an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). The FAA intends to award up to eight (8) OTAs through this solicitation. BEYOND Phase 2 has four programmatic focus areas: infrastructure, scalability, safety and automation. Five operational focus areas have also been identified as the greatest challenges that will need to be addressed for progress to be made: public safety, controlled airspace, remote, rural areas with inadequate infrastructure, on-airport operations and cross international borders. This SIR is seeking Offerors who can deliver successful outcomesin support of the BEYOND Phase 2 focus areas. See SIR for details. The FAA intends to competitively award up to eight (8) Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) with SLTTs in accordance with the SIR. The FAA reserves the right to execute additional OTAs if resources permit (49 U.S.C. � 106(l)). The Government will make OTA awards to the Offeror�s determined to best meet the selection criteria which are included in this SIR and reflected in the evaluation of the proposals. To be considered for award of this requirement, the Offeror must have a current/valid registration in the Systems for Award Management (SAM) database website: www.sam.gov. Registration must be active by the offer due date. Proposals must be submitted via email to the Contracting Officer and Contract Specialist no later than 3:00 pm ET on September 10, 2026. Please see attached SIR for proposal submission requirements. Questions are to be submitted, in writing, as specified in the SIR. Please reference the SIR number and BEYOND Phase 2 program on all question submissions. All questions must be received no later than 1:00pm ET on September 3, 2026. Questions will be answered in an Amendment to the SIR if deemed necessary and posted to SAM.GOV for all interested parties to consider. Prospective Offerors are encouraged to frequently visit SAM.GOV for any updates to this requirement. Any questions regarding this announcement should be directed to Kristin Frantz, Contracting Officer, at Kristin.T.Frantz@faa.gov and Jackson LeMay, Contract Specialist, at Jackson.T.Lemay@faa.gov Any proposals received after the closing date and time, will not be considered in accordance with this SIR. The Government will not be liable for payment of any costs attributed to the preparation and submission of requested proposal documentation.

title: Multi-Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center, Lackland Air Force Base, Texas
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Fort Worth District, on behalf of the Department of the Air Force (DAF), is issuing this solicitation announcement to identify a Design-Build (DB) team for a new Multi-Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center (MDCIOC) at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA), Lackland AFB, Texas. The proposed project involves the design and construction of an approximately 600,000-square-foot, multi-story facility to consolidate the 16th Air Force's Information Warfare workforce. The new center will be a state-of-the-art, 24/7 facility designed to the highest security and technical standards, including ICD 705. The project will house over 3,000 personnel and support global cyberspace operations, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR). The project delivery model will be a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) executed through an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement. The acquisition will be conducted in two phases: Phase 1: Design and Pre-Construction Services: The selected DB team will collaborate with the Government to advance the design and refine project requirements. Phase 2: Full Design and Construction: Upon successful negotiation of a fair and reasonable price, the OT may be modified to include the final design and construction. The Government will use a two-step, qualifications-based selection process: White Paper Submission & Evaluation. Pitch Meetings (by invitation only). Request for White Papers: Interested parties are invited to submit a White Paper in accordance with this announcement and its attachments. The White Paper is the only submission required at this time and must address all requirements outlined in Attachment 1 of the solicitation to be considered. Submissions should demonstrate the respondent's qualifications, project understanding, and relevant experience. Questions Due Date: All questions must be submitted via the ProjNet Bidder Inquiry System by September 18, 2026, in accordance with the instructions in the solicitation. White Paper Due Date: White Papers must be submitted via email to the Solicitation POCs no later than 2:00 PM CT on September 25, 2026. Email Subject Line: "White Paper for Multi Domain Cyber & Intel Operations Center" Please refer to the attached solicitation document and Attachments for complete details on the project scope, submission requirements, and evaluation criteria.

All products must be Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved. The products that make up the �procedural packages� must be delivered Just-In-Time (JIT), Direct Vendor Delivery (DVD) and Consignment. Under the JIT delivery method, the Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) calls the manufacturer�s field representative who carries the products into the MTF just-in-time for the surgery. The manufacturer�s sales representative may bring many sizes and types of implants and other auxiliary products to the surgery along with the instrumentation sets. Under the DVD method an order for products is placed through ECAT and the products are delivered directly to the customer via any transportation carrier. Under the consignment method a Medical Treatment Facility (MTF) will have the products that make up the �procedural package� consigned to their facility. At the request of the MTF�s, the manufacturer is required to have a qualified representative on site at the MTF�s within the timeframe specified by the facility necessary to meet their requirements. The manufacturer�s representative�s provides technical advice and guidance to the physician�s before, during and after implantation.
